title_protection.quote: No person other than the holder of a valid existing license under this Act shall use the title and designation of "Doctor of Optometry", "O.D.", or "optometrist", either directly or indirectly in connection with his or her profession or business.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violations of the Optometric Practice Act or rules promulgated thereunder.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violations of this Act, or of the rules promulgated hereunder.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction of or plea of guilty to a felony, a misdemeanor involving dishonesty, or a crime directly related to the practice of the profession.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction of or entry of a plea of guilty to any crime under the laws of any U.S. jurisdiction thereof that is a felony or that is a misdemeanor of which an essential element is dishonesty, or any crime that is directly related to the practice of the profession.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Making any misrepresentation for the purpose of obtaining a license.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Making any misrepresentation for the purpose of obtaining a license.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Professional incompetence or gross negligence in the practice of optometry.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Professional incompetence or gross negligence in the practice of optometry.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Gross malpractice, as evidenced by a conviction or judgment of malpractice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Gross malpractice, prima facie evidence of which may be a conviction or judgment of malpractice in any court of competent jurisdiction.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Aiding or assisting another person in violating any provision of the Act or rules.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Aiding or assisting another person in violating any provision of this Act or rules.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failing within 60 days to provide information in response to a written request made by the Department.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failing, within 60 days, to provide information in response to a written request made by the Department that has been sent by certified or registered mail to the licensee's last known address.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Engaging in dishonorable, unethical, or unprofessional conduct likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Engaging in dishonorable, unethical, or unprofessional conduct of a character likely to deceive, defraud, or harm the public.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Habitual or excessive use or addiction to alcohol, narcotics, stimulants, or any chemical agent resulting in inability to practice safely.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Habitual or excessive use or addiction to alcohol, narcotics, stimulants or any other chemical agent or drug that results in the inability to practice with reasonable judgment, skill, or safety.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Discipline by another US jurisdiction or foreign nation for grounds substantially equivalent to those in this Act.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Discipline by another U.S. jurisdiction or foreign nation, if at least one of the grounds for the discipline is the same or substantially equivalent to those set forth herein.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of the prohibition against fee splitting in Section 24.2 of the Act.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation of the prohibition against fee splitting in Section 24.2 of this Act.

disciplinary_grounds.description: A finding that the licensee on probationary status has violated the terms of probation.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A finding by the Department that the licensee, after having his or her license placed on probationary status has violated the terms of probation.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Abandonment of a patient.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Abandonment of a patient.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willfully making or filing false records or reports in practice, including records filed with state agencies.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willfully making or filing false records or reports in his or her practice, including but not limited to false records filed with State agencies or departments.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willfully failing to report an instance of suspected abuse or neglect as required by law.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willfully failing to report an instance of suspected abuse or neglect as required by law.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Physical illness, aging, mental illness, or disability resulting in inability to practice with reasonable judgment, skill, or safety.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Physical illness, including but not limited to, deterioration through the aging process, or loss of motor skill, mental illness, or disability that results in the inability to practice the profession with reasonable judgment, skill, or safety.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Solicitation of professional services other than permitted advertising.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Solicitation of professional services other than permitted advertising.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to provide a patient with a copy of their record or prescription in accordance with federal law.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to provide a patient with a copy of his or her record or prescription in accordance with federal law.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Conviction by any court of violation of any law governing the practice of optometry, or of a felony in this or another state.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Conviction by any court of competent jurisdiction, either within or without this State, of any violation of any law governing the practice of optometry

disciplinary_grounds.description: A finding that licensure has been applied for or obtained by fraudulent means.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A finding that licensure has been applied for or obtained by fraudulent means.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Continued practice by a person knowingly having an infectious or contagious disease.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Continued practice by a person knowingly having an infectious or contagious disease.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Being named as a perpetrator in an indicated report of child abuse or neglect.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Being named as a perpetrator in an indicated report by the Department of Children and Family Services under the Abused and Neglected Child Reporting Act

disciplinary_grounds.description: Practicing or attempting to practice under a name other than the full name as shown on the license.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing or attempting to practice under a name other than the full name as shown on his or her license.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Immoral conduct in the commission of any act such as sexual abuse, sexual misconduct, or sexual exploitation related to the licensee's practice.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Immoral conduct in the commission of any act, such as sexual abuse, sexual misconduct or sexual exploitation, related to the licensee's practice.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Maintaining a professional relationship with any person, firm, or corporation the optometrist knows is violating the Act.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Maintaining a professional relationship with any person, firm, or corporation when the optometrist knows, or should know, that such person, firm, or corporation is violating this Act.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Promoting the sale of drugs, devices, appliances or goods in a manner that exploits the patient for financial gain.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Promotion of the sale of drugs, devices, appliances or goods provided for a client or patient in such manner as to exploit the patient or client for financial gain of the licensee.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Using the title 'Doctor' or its abbreviation without further qualifying it with the word 'optometry' or 'optometrist'.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Using the title "Doctor" or its abbreviation without further qualifying that title or abbreviation with the word "optometry" or "optometrist".

disciplinary_grounds.description: Use of terms like 'infirmary', 'hospital', 'school', 'university' in connection with the optometric practice location unless employed at a licensed hospital or accredited institution.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Use by a licensed optometrist of the word "infirmary", "hospital", "school", "university", in English or any other language, in connection with the place where optometry may be practiced

disciplinary_grounds.description: Continuing in the employ of a person, firm, or corporation after the employer has been found guilty of or enjoined from violating optometry laws and persists in violation.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Continuance of an optometrist in the employ of any person, firm or corporation ... after his or her employer or superior has been found guilty of violating or has been enjoined from violating the laws of the State of Illinois relating to the practice of optometry, when the employer or superior persists in that violation.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Performance of optometric service in conjunction with a scheme or plan with a person, firm, or corporation advertising in a manner contrary to the Act.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The performance of optometric service in conjunction with a scheme or plan with another person, firm or corporation known to be advertising in a manner contrary to this Act

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to provide satisfactory proof of having participated in approved continuing education programs.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to provide satisfactory proof of having participated in approved continuing education programs as determined by the Board and approved by the Secretary.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Willfully making or filing false records or reports in optometric practice, including false statements for collection of Medicaid fees.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Willfully making or filing false records or reports in the practice of optometry, including, but not limited to false records to support claims against the medical assistance program

disciplinary_grounds.description: Gross and willful overcharging for professional services, including filing false statements for collection of fees for services not rendered.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Gross and willful overcharging for professional services including filing false statements for collection of fees for which services are not rendered

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to perform a minimum eye examination as required by the rules of the Department, absent good reason.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: In the absence of good reasons to the contrary, failure to perform a minimum eye examination as required by the rules of the Department.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Violation of the Health Care Worker Self-Referral Act.
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Violation of the Health Care Worker Self-Referral Act.

definition_quote.value: The practice of optometry is defined as the employment of any and all means for the examination, diagnosis, and treatment of the human visual system, the human eye, and its appendages without the use of surgery, including, but not limited to: the appropriate use of ocular pharmaceutical agents; refraction and other determinants of visual function; prescribing corrective lenses or prisms; prescribing, dispensing, or management of contact lenses; vision therapy; visual rehabilitation; or any other procedures taught in schools and colleges of optometry approved by the Department, and not specifically restricted in this Act

drug_authority.value: Licensed optometrists may use topical anesthetics, topical mydriatics, topical cycloplegics, topical miotics and mydriatic reversing agents, anti-infective agents, anti-allergy agents, anti-glaucoma agents (except oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors limited to 30-day supply), anti-inflammatory agents (except oral steroids limited to 7-day supply), over-the-counter agents, analgesic agents, anti-dry eye agents, agents for treatment of hypotrichosis. Ocular pharmaceutical agents by injection only for anaphylaxis. Schedule III, IV, V controlled substances for analgesics limited to 72-hour supply; Schedule II prohibited except Hydrocodone combinations if reclassified, limited to 72 hours.
drug_authority.quote: "ocular pharmaceutical agents" means topical anesthetics, topical mydriatics, topical cycloplegics, topical miotics and mydriatic reversing agents, anti-infective agents, anti-allergy agents, anti-glaucoma agents (except oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, which may be prescribed only in a quantity sufficient to provide treatment for up to 30 days), anti-inflammatory agents (except oral steroids, which may be prescribed only in a quantity sufficient to provide treatment for up to 7 days), over-the-counter agents, analgesic agents, anti-dry eye agents, and agents for the treatment of hypotrichosis.

surgery_prohibited.quote: The practice of optometry is defined as the employment of any and all means for the examination, diagnosis, and treatment of the human visual system, the human eye, and its appendages without the use of surgery

foreign_body_removal_authorized.quote: A licensed optometrist may remove superficial foreign bodies from the human eye and adnexa

laser_procedures_authorized.quote: Advanced optometric procedures do not include the use of lasers.

value: removal of superficial foreign bodies from the human eye and adnexa
advanced optometric procedures (per certification from approved school, excluding lasers)
minor_surgical_procedures_authorized.quote: A licensed optometrist may remove superficial foreign bodies from the human eye and adnexa and may give orders for patient care to a nurse or other health care provider licensed to practice under Illinois law.

glaucoma_treatment_authorized.quote: anti-glaucoma agents (except oral carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, which may be prescribed only in a quantity sufficient to provide treatment for up to 30 days)

anaphylaxis_treatment_authorized.quote: Ocular pharmaceutical agents administered by injection may be used only for the treatment of anaphylaxis.

immunization_authority.quote: A licensed optometrist may independently administer the COVID-19 vaccine upon the completion of appropriate training
